_comment: Every secret this project holds, by PATH and ROLE — never by value. ops/SECRETS.md is the policy and the reasoning; this file is the list, so the two cannot drift. ops/check-secret-age.mjs reads it: a secret past its rotation interval fails, and so does one that has stopped being ignored by git, which is the failure that actually loses money. `rotateDays: null` means a key whose rotation is a migration rather than a refresh — see the note, and SECRETS.md's section on why some keys cannot be rotated at all.

secrets.holds: the funder and principal of nearly every grant issued so far
can: receive the balance of any grant it is principal of
secrets.note: Cannot be rotated in the useful sense. A grant hashes its keys into its address, so the 29 grants naming this key as principal name it forever. Replacing the file makes a NEW key; it does not move the old one's authority. See ops/PRINCIPAL.md.

secrets.holds: the revocation key for grants issued since 16 September
can: stop any grant that names it
receive nothing — revoke pays the principal
secrets.note: Same: fixed at each grant's genesis. Deliberately allowed to be warmer than the principal, which is the whole reason the two roles exist.

can: fund grants automatically, bounded only by its own balance
secrets.note: The only bound on unattended issuance is what this key holds — ops/auto-issue.sh refuses to run against the main funder for exactly that reason. Rotating means moving the float to a new key and updating the script; nothing on chain refers to it.

secrets.holds: the Telegram bot token, the console cron secret and the admin secret
secrets.note: The bot token was leaked into a conversation on 23 September by a shell idiom that printed the value instead of testing it. Rotate in BotFather (/revoke then /token), then update this file. Nothing on chain depends on it; the alerts go quiet until the file is updated.

can: read X on our billing account
secrets.note: The bearer token was leaked in the same message as the Telegram one, and it bills to our card — a leak here is somebody else's usage on our account. Rotate in the X developer portal. QUOTE_SECRET must NOT be rotated casually: growth/RUNBOOK.md says it has to be stable for the life of the process, because regenerating it invalidates every outstanding quote.
Same constraint as the Listener's: stable for the life of the process. Rotating invalidates outstanding quotes, so it is done at a restart with none in flight.

can: whatever its scopes allow on this account
secrets.note: Check the scopes when rotating. A token minted for one script tends to outlive the script.

secrets.holds: DATABASE_URL, the Turnkey organisation id and key file path, and three shared secrets
can: read and write the runner's database
authenticate tick, signup and admin calls
secrets.note: The Neon password in DATABASE_URL was pasted into a conversation and must be rotated in the Neon console before anything here touches real money. The Turnkey credential is separate — see MAINNET.md 3.4, where the deployed policy is broader than runner/DESIGN.md says it should be.

can: name a machine we do not want strangers using as their RPC provider
secrets.note: Not a credential. Ignored because publishing it invites load, not because it authorises anything.

_agent_keys: The per-agent and per-demo keys — covenant/deploy/agent-00N.key, growth/keys/*.key, one-job*/keys/*.key, site/agent.key, site/wallet.key, agent-005/agent.key, v5-demo/coord.key — are deliberately NOT listed individually. Each one is bounded by the covenant: it spends inside a grant's limits and can do nothing else, which is the entire claim this protocol makes. They are the keys a leak is supposed to be survivable for, and /attack publishes one on purpose. Rotating them means issuing a new grant, which is the same operation as retiring an agent.
_compromised: `compromised` is the day a credential is known to have been exposed. It stays overdue until `rotatedAt` is set to a later day BY HAND, not until the file's mtime moves — because an mtime moves for every reason under the sun. runner/.env was rewritten on 22 September for a fee-payee change, three days after the Neon password went into a chat window, and a check keyed on mtime would have called that rotated. Setting rotatedAt is somebody saying they did the thing, which is the only signal worth having here.
